cardboard.name: Cardboard
prep_steps: Flatten and break down boxes to conserve bin volume.
Remove plastic packing tape, styrofoam, and bubble wrap inserts.
Ensure cardboard is clean; heavily grease-stained parts belong in compost or general waste.
cardboard.environmental_impact: Recycling 1 ton of cardboard saves 17 mature trees, 7,000 gallons of water, and 4,000 kWh of energy.
cardboard.common_items: Shipping cartons, cereal & shoe boxes, corrugated packaging, paper towel tubes.

glass.name: Glass Container
prep_steps: Empty and rinse containers to remove food remnants and residues.
Remove corks and metal screw-caps (metal caps can be recycled separately).
Keep whole. Broken drinking glasses, window panes, and mirrors should be placed in General Trash due to different melting points.
glass.environmental_impact: Glass can be recycled endlessly with zero degradation in purity or strength. Recycled glass reduces kiln temperatures and lowers CO2 emissions by up to 30%.
glass.common_items: Soda & beverage bottles, sauce jars, condiment bottles, cosmetic jars.

metal.name: Metal & Cans
prep_steps: Rinse food and beverage cans clean of residue.
Crush aluminum cans if convenient to optimize bin space.
Paper labels do not need to be removed; they burn away cleanly in smelting furnaces.
metal.environmental_impact: Recycling a single aluminum can saves 95% of the energy needed to make a new one from raw bauxite ore—saving enough energy to power a laptop for 5 hours.
metal.common_items: Aluminum beverage cans, tin soup/pet food cans, clean aluminum foil & trays, metal lids.

paper.name: Paper Waste
prep_steps: Keep clean and dry; moisture and oil spoil paper fiber recycling.
Remove heavy plastic sleeves, wax coatings, and metal ring binders.
Staples are acceptable; industrial pulpers filter them out automatically.
paper.environmental_impact: Recycling 1 ton of paper saves 17 trees, 3 cubic yards of landfill space, and 380 gallons of oil.
paper.common_items: Office paper, newspapers, magazines, brochures, envelopes, paper bags, notebooks.

plastic.name: Plastic Container
prep_steps: Empty all liquids and rinse container clean.
Squash or flatten bottles to minimize bin volume.
Check resin identification codes (numbers #1 and #2 have the highest recycling value).
plastic.environmental_impact: Recycling plastic conserves crude oil, reduces greenhouse emissions by 67%, and prevents harmful microplastics from polluting terrestrial and marine ecosystems.
plastic.common_items: Water bottles, detergent jugs, shampoo bottles, yogurt containers, milk jugs.

trash.name: Non-Recyclable Waste
prep_steps: Bag waste securely to prevent litter and odor dispersion.
Ensure no batteries, chemical solvents, or electronics are mixed in (deliver to e-waste depots).
Evaluate whether single-use products can be substituted with durable, reusable alternatives in the future.
trash.environmental_impact: Residual waste sent to landfills breaks down anaerobically and produces methane gas. Diligent sorting redirects valuable raw materials away from landfills.
trash.common_items: Soiled food wrappers, greasy chip bags, broken ceramics, dirty tissues, multi-material pouches.
